newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals mixed in thin trade.

text.p: Regional currencies were mixed on Wednesday with trading subdued ahead of the 0930 GMT speech by Eisuke Sakakibara of Japan's Ministry of Finance.
The Indonesian rupiah firmed slightly against the dollar after a weaker open, with the focus on liquidity due to the new bank reserve requirement rate, effective on Wednesday.
Dealers were worried whether the market could absorb the fall-out of the new reserve rate, which is estimated to drain between five and eight trillion rupiah from the system.
"We feel a light increase in rupiah demand. But dollar supplies seem to be enough," a Japanese bank dealer said, adding he did not detect any rush to buy today dollars.
"We saw some uptrend in the morning. Overnight money is crawling up, thus driving the dollar a bit lower," a dealer based in Jakarta said.
"We haven't got a clear picture yet. People are trying to test the market first," he said, adding that early injection of 3.359 trillion rupiah by the central bank helped calm operators.
At 0400 GMT, spot rupiah was at 2,407.75/08.25 compared with an opening of 2,407.5/08.5.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,401/2,593 and the conversion band to 2,401/2,449 on Tuesday.
Dealers in Singapore pegged rupiah support and resistance at 2,407 and 2,408.75 to a dollar.
The Thai market resumed trading after a four day public holiday but a directionless dollar/yen market limited trading.
The Thai baht weakened against the dollar as the greenback made marginal gains against the Japanese currency, dealers said.
At 0400 GMT, the baht was at 26.084/089 a dollar against 26.067-26.072 late on Friday.
The central bank set the midrate at 26.09 baht per dollar.
"There may be little selling (of baht) this morning because people think the dollar trend is going stronger against yen," said a dealer at Siam City Bank Plc.
Liquidity was expected to tighten as banks prepared to meet central bank reserve requirements on April 22 and finance firms were due to meet their reserve requirements on Thursday.
Ringgit sales from U.S. funds pushed the ringgit to test 2.5120 for a second time, but dollar sales from Kuala Lumpur prevented a decline, dealers said.
"Some people are simply buying up dollar/ringgit. It seems like someone is building a huge position against ringgit since last week," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore.
He said some U.S. funds, mostly margin players, were involved in the dollar accumulation. "The position could be a few yards (billion dollars)," he added.
Ringgit hit a low of 2.5140 a dollar overnight on selling in London, but fell back on rumours that Bank Negara was selling dollars, dealers said. About $30-40 million was traded.
"Stop-losses at 2.5120 increased activity in London time and brought down dollar/ringgit," a Malaysian bank dealer said.
Singapore dollar was range-bound at 1.4405/35 to the U.S. currency. One chartist said if the Singapore dollar were to breaks 1.4450, 1.4530 would be re-tested.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), James Mclean in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Angela Tan in Singapore (65-8703083)
